sources.citation: Michailovsky, Boyd (n.d.). Notes on the Kiranti Verb (East Nepal). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 2.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Part I (pp. 5-24) is a morphophonological study of Bahing verb-root finals and vocalism. Its phonology outline lists initials, clusters, finals, ten vowels with distinctive length and nasality, and syllable/word structure, and says nothing about stress, accent, pitch or tone in Bahing;txt) for stress/accent/tone/pitch/prosod/intonation finds no Bahing hit. The only tone content is Part II on Khaling. First-hand: 'The present study is based on field work carried out by Martine Mazaudon and myself in Rangadip

sources.citation: Michailovsky, Boyd. 2017. Kiranti languages. In Thurgood & LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 2nd ed. Routledge (author MS, HAL halshs-01705023).
sources.note: Sec. 2.5 'Tone, Stress': fixed stress named for Belhare, Dumi, Wambule; stress opposition in Sangpang; Bahing not mentioned for stress or tone (only: length pertinent on open syllables only).

sources.note: Morphosyntax only; no phonology. (Nepalese Linguistics vols 21-34 text-searched: only this article plus bibliographic mentions; vol. 22 with Thokar 2006 'Case marking in Bahing' is image-only, not scanned.)

sources.citation: Lee, Maureen. 2011. Issues in Bahing orthography development. Himalayan Linguistics 10(1): 227-252. doi:10.5070/H910123575
sources.note: Orthography paper (implosive, glottal stop, dialectal vowels, vowel length incl. length of possessive prefixes conditioned by stem syllable count, sec. 2.4); no statement about stress or tone.

sources.citation: Michailovsky, Boyd. 1988. Phonological typology of Nepal languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 11(2): 25-50.
sources.note: Areal survey including Bahing (Rangadip): Bahing non-tonal; long vowels 'restricted.. to non-final syllables (Bahing, Jirel..)'; length secondary from lost finals. The word 'stress' does not occur in the paper; nothing on Bahing accent.

sources.citation: Michailovsky, Boyd. 1975. Notes on the Kiranti verb (East Nepal). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 2(2): 183-218. Part I 'The Bahing verb' pp. 185-214 (Rangadip dialect, fieldwork 1973).
sources.note: Sec. 1 'Outline of Bahing phonology' (pp. 185-186) gives initials, clusters, finals, ten vowels, 'length and nasality are distinctive', syllable (C(C))V(C); p.187 open-syllable length neutralized word-finally. No mention of stress or accent anywhere; tone is discussed only for Khaling (Part II).

sources.citation: Pangloss Collection, Bahing corpus page and transcription notes (Mazaudon & Michailovsky 1973 texts, rev. 2005).
sources.note: Notes on 10 vowels, distinctive vowel length, implosive; nothing on stress or tone. No Bahing dictionary online at Pangloss.

sources.citation: Hodgson, Brian H. 1880 [1857-58]. Miscellaneous essays relating to Indian subjects, vol. 1, sect. IV 'Analysis of the Bahing dialect of the Kiranti language', pp. 320-392 (= JASB 26: 486-522; 27: 393-442). London: Truebner.
sources.note: No phonology section; vocabulary + paradigms. Acute accent in Hodgson's system marks 'the graver or lengthened sound' of a vowel (p.72); footnotes distinguish an 'abrupt tone' (h', standing for a dropped consonant) vs a 'pausing tone' (doubled vowel), e.g. to'mi 'he strikes' vs to'ome 'he places' — glottal closure/length, not word-stress placement.
sources.venue: Miscellaneous essays relating to Indian subjects

tone.quote: Observation on the Distribution of Phonemes (a) The alveolar stop sounds are not available in Kiranti-Bayung whereas in Kiranti-Kõits they are phonemic though not very productive. (b) The initial stops of the velar and bilabial series may be followed by /r/ or /l/ to form initial consonant clusters. (c) The system of syllable- final consonants in Kiranti-Bayung is /p/, /t/, /k/, /m/, /n/, / ŋ/, /r/, /l/, /s/, zero. (d) There are eleven vowels, as shown in Table 2. (e) Syllables may also begin with a vowel (zero consonant initail).
tone.locator: Unit II, sec. 2.1 'Phonological Sketch', pp. 13-14; the sketch runs pp. 11-15 and contains no suprasegmental paragraph
